title: Hand the correct screw
instruction: The person asks for an M4 x 20 mm Phillips pan-head machine screw. Take one screw from the bin whose front label reads M4 and place it in their open palm; then let go.
context: Hardware-counter and bench-assembly work: a helper must match a spoken size request to a labeled bin, pick one fastener, and hand it over without grabbing the wrong size. Done by retail salespersons, stock clerks and assemblers (O*NET 41-2031.00, 53-7065.00, 51-2092.00). The bins look alike; only the printed size mark identifies the correct part.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases on the table (x forward away from the robot, y to the robot's left). Three open bins in a row, long axis left-right, centres at x 28, y -12 / 0 / 12: each bin is a rigid light-grey PLA box, outside 8 x 6 x 4 cm tall, walls 4 mm thick, open top, with a white paper label 3 x 1.5 cm glued flat on the front (robot-facing) wall. Left to right the labels read in 12 mm black sans-serif: M3, M4, M5. Inside each bin, three steel Phillips pan-head machine screws lie loose, threaded shanks parallel to y, heads toward +x: the M3 bin holds three M3 x 16 mm screws (head 5.5 mm dia, 2 mm tall; shank 3 mm dia, 16 mm long under the head; 1.6 g each); the M4 bin three M4 x 20 mm (head 7 mm dia, 2.5 mm tall; shank 4 mm dia, 20 mm; 3.1 g each); the M5 bin three M5 x 25 mm (head 8.5 mm dia, 3 mm tall; shank 5 mm dia, 25 mm; 5.4 g each). All screws are bare steel, no washers. A fixed tan PLA forearm and open right palm (person's right = robot's left) sits at x 18, y 22: palm pad a flat disc 9 cm dia, 1.5 cm thick, face up at table height + 2 cm, centre marked with a 2 cm black circle; the forearm is a 4 x 4 x 18 cm block running from the palm toward +y. A white request card 6 x 4 cm fixed on a 2 cm stand at x 12, y 22 reads M4 x 20 mm in 10 mm black type, facing the robot. The right arm starts nearer the bins; the left nearer the palm.
scoring: End state only, after the arms stop, from a top photo and a caliper or the scorer's pose readouts. Score 0 if: any gripper centre is within 3 cm of any screw; more than one screw lies on the palm; any screw from the M3 or M5 bin lies on the palm; the bins, palm, forearm or request card were moved more than 1 cm from their marks; a bin tip exceeds 15 degrees. A screw lies on the palm when its centre is inside the 9 cm palm disc (top view), its lowest point is within 4 mm of the palm's top face, and it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Otherwise: 0.25 if any single M4 screw has been lifted at least 3 cm above the table at any point; 0.5 if exactly one M4 screw lies on the palm but a second screw of any size also touches the palm or the forearm; 1.0 if exactly one M4 x 20 mm screw lies alone on the palm, released, at rest for 1 s, and the other eight screws remain in their starting bins (each screw's centre still inside its bin's inner 7.2 x 5.2 cm floor outline). Partial credit is not additive beyond those tiers.
reset_notes: Return every screw to its labeled bin (three M3, three M4, three M5), shanks along y, heads toward +x. Check the three bin labels face the robot and the request card still shows M4 x 20 mm. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate: screw threads are not modeled (plain cylinders under a disc head); Phillips recesses are visual only. Labels are flat textures, not OCR-scored—the scorer identifies screws by which bin they started in and by measured diameter. The person is a fixed forearm and palm with no grasp or motion. All contacts use one rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Real setup: printed bins with printed labels, real metric machine screws, a fixed manikin hand or a flat disc taped as the palm.
